'''Srinivas Kishanrao Saidapur''' (born 17 July 1947) is an Indian reproductive biologist, academic and a former vice chancellor of [[Karnatak University]].<ref name="Dr S K Saidapur to be new VC of Karnatak University">{{cite web | url=http://www.oneindia.com/2006/10/24/dr-s-k-saidapur-to-be-new-vc-of-karnatak-university-1161744503.html | title=Dr S K Saidapur to be new VC of Karnatak University | publisher=One India | date=25 October 2006 | accessdate=5 October 2016}}</ref> He is known for his studies on comparative endocrinology of amphibians and the reproductive biology of the [[vertebrates]]<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/content/Detail.aspx?AID=26 | title=Brief Profile of the Awardee | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | accessdate=5 October 2016}}</ref> and is an elected fellow of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]], [[Indian National Science Academy]], [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] and [[The World Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="Indian Fellow - Saidapur">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N94-1160 | title=Indian Fellow - Saidapur | publisher=Indian National Science Academy | date=2016 | accessdate=5 October 2016}}</ref> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1991, for his contributions to biological sciences.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | accessdate=5 October 2016}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Srinivas Saidapur, born on 17 July 1947 in the [[South Indian]] state of [[Karnataka]], did all his college education, except the post-doctoral studies, at [[Karnatak University]] from where he secured his graduate, master's and doctoral degrees.<ref name="Indian Fellow - Saidapur" /> After completing his master's degree, he joined the university as a lecturer of zoology in 1972 and spent his entire academic career there, superannuating in 2010. In between, he obtained his PhD in 1974 and did his post-doctoral studies at [[University of Kansas Hospital]] during 1976–79 and on an [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Alexander von Humboldt Fellowship]], he did research at [[University of Mainz]] during 1989–90. At Karnatak University, he served as a professor from 1988 till he was appointed as the vice chancellor of the university in 2006, a post he held till 2010.<ref name="Former VCs">{{cite web | url=http://www.kud.ac.in/content.aspx?module=about&page=about | title=Former VCs | publisher=Karnatak University | date=2016 | accessdate=5 October 2016}}</ref> He also served as a visiting scientist at the [[National Institute for Basic Biology, Japan]] and had two short stints in Germany at [[Ruhr University Bochum]] in 1995 and [[University of Würzburg]] in 2004 as an INSA-DFG Exchange Program fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]] and [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft]] (DFG).<ref name="Indian Fellow - Saidapur" />

Focusing his researches on [[comparative endocrinology]] of amphibians, Saidapur explained the different types of reproductive processes followed by the tropical [[List of Anuran families|anurans]] and their control mechanisms.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=1999 | accessdate=5 October 2016 | pages=35}}</ref> His studies are reported to have widened the understanding of the reproductive biology of the [[vertebrates]] and concentrating his researches on [[Indian Bullfrog]], he proposed [[gametogenesis]] methodologies for producing frogs of predetermined sex.<ref name="Indian Fellow - Saidapur" /> His studies also covered the [[behavioral ecology]] of anuran [[tadpoles]] and [[Agama (lizard)|agamid lizards]] with regard to their [[foraging]] techniques, food identification, [[Kin recognition|kin detection]] and predator-prey relationships and he developed new ways for the [[captive breeding]] of reptiles. On the academic front, it was under his leadership Karnatak University introduced new academic courses on [[molecular biology]], [[animal behavior]] and [[evolutionary biology]]. He is a former member of the INSA council and served as its vice president during 2012–14.<ref name="Recent Past Vice-presidents">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.res.in/recent_past_office_bearers.php | title=Recent Past Vice-presidents | publisher=Indian National Science Academy | date=2016 | accessdate=5 October 2016}}</ref> He has also published several articles{{Refn|group=note|Please see Selected bibliography section}} and has mentored 13 scholars in their doctoral researches.<ref name="Indian Fellow - Saidapur" />

== Awards and honors ==
The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] awarded Saidapur the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1991. Two years later, the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] elected him as a fellow<ref name="Fellow profile - Saidapur">{{cite web | url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Saidapur,_Prof._Srinivas_Kishanrao | title=Fellow profile - Saidapur | publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences | date=2016 | accessdate=6 October 2016}}</ref> and the [[Indian National Science Academy]] followed suit, a year later. He received the fellowships of the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]]<ref name="NASI fellows">{{cite web | url=http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=S | title=NASI fellows | publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India | date=2016 | accessdate=6 October 2016}}</ref> and [[The World Academy of Sciences]] in 2009 and 2010 respectively.<ref name="TWAS fellows">{{cite web | url=http://twas.org/member/saidapur-srinivas-k | title=TWAS fellows | publisher=The World Academy of Sciences | date=2016 | accessdate=6 October 2016}}</ref> He has also delivered many award orations which included the 2007 Professor MRN Prasad Memorial Lecture and 2010 Professor Har Swarup Memorial Lecture.<ref name="Endowment lectures">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.res.in/aa3.php | title=Endowment lectures | publisher=INSA | date=2016 | accessdate=5 October 2016}}</ref>
